lines.trans: Yes, Viktoria Sergeyevna, did you call me?
Kostya, explain what this mess in the bar is?
There is no terrible mess here.
Why was a strange man standing behind the bar counter?
He is a specialist and was fixing our electronic register.
You left a stranger completely alone without supervision?
I stepped away to the kitchen for literally a minute.
And now look carefully at this shelf.
I see nothing unusual here.
Where then is our expensive cognac standing?
This cognac always stood right here.
The bottle is no longer in its place.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Вы можете подождать за барной стойкой.
examples.trans: You can wait at the bar counter.

examples.text: Что ты вообще делаешь за нашей барной стойкой?
examples.trans: What are you even doing behind our bar counter?

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'порядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'disorder, disturbance' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: To cause disturbances on the street.
There is complete disorder in the room.

examples.text: Он устроил беспорядки прямо на городской улице.
examples.trans: He caused disturbances right on the city street.
We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.
They beat me literally every day!
With a bottle of wine in your hand?

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
to a loved one, and at the start of letters
to a loved one, and at the start of letters

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: звать на помощь = to call for help
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: device or station for recording payments and holding money

examples.trans: The waiter approached the cash register.
Where is the restaurant cash register?

examples.text: Он подошёл к кассе оплатить счёт.
examples.trans: He stepped up to the cash desk to pay the bill.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: A mysterious stranger entered the bar.

examples.text: Ты оставил незнакомца совсем одного без присмотра?
examples.trans: You left a stranger completely alone without supervision?

meanings.note: remarkable or different from the ordinary

examples.text: Я не вижу здесь ничего необычного.
Да, она такая необычная и красивая.
examples.trans: Yes, it is so unusual and beautiful.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: оставь мне кусок = save me a piece
оставь мне кусок = save me a piece

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step aside, to move back

examples.trans: He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!

examples.text: Возьми хорошую бутылку на верхней полке.
examples.trans: Take a good bottle on the top shelf.

examples.text: А теперь внимательно посмотри на эту полку.
examples.trans: And now look carefully at this shelf.

examples.text: Мы проверили все столы и полки.
examples.trans: We checked all tables and shelves.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Ты оставил незнакомца совсем одного без присмотра?
examples.trans: You left a stranger completely alone without supervision?

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

examples.text: Костя протёр барную стойку чистым полотенцем.
examples.trans: Kostya wiped the bar counter with a clean towel.

examples.text: Вы можете подождать за барной стойкой.
examples.trans: You can wait at the bar counter.

examples.text: Ты разлил молоко на всю стойку!
examples.trans: You spilled milk all over the counter!

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fix, to repair', paired with 'починить'.

examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?
An electronic bracelet on the leg.

examples.text: Я уже носил этот электронный браслет.
examples.trans: I have already worn this electronic bracelet.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
